content:
Nina: Heads-up — got a noisy pager storm this morning where CPU spikes on routing instances bubbled into a cascade of alerts and a couple of customer timeouts. I want to schedule a short post-incident to capture the mitigations and land a small runbook edit: clarify signal thresholds, add an immediate reroute step, and tighten escalation timings.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-314 · paging spike · severity=sev2 · affected=api-routing · started=2026-03-15T08:12Z

Carlos: tl;dr mitigation we did: scaled the routing pool, flipped traffic to warm fallback region, and temporarily increased the per-instance token cap to reduce head-of-line backpressure. The immediate fix worked but we had ambiguous paging noise — two different alerts triggered separate on-calls.

Jo: Customer impact — we saw ~7k requests with 5xx over a 9m window. Top customers affected: onboarding-test, report-generator (internal). No live revenue hits reported but perceptible latency blips for end-users behind the routing tier.

Priya: Sending the graphs here: https://redwood.corp/graphs/INC-2026-314 (mock link). From the traces it looks like the spike originated from a malformed bulk-batch job that hit a hot partition, caused KV cache churn and CPU scheduling delays.

Eli: Recommendation: add a deterministic reroute step in the runbook so that when a routing node CPU > 70% and error rate > 3% for 2m, we immediately move the affected customer prefixes to fallback region and open a canary route. That avoids duplicate pages and reduces manual coordination.

Nina: Agree. Proposed minimal runbook patch (draft):

```
Title: routing-hotspot-quick-reroute
Trigger: routing-node CPU > 70% AND error_rate > 3% over 120s
Steps:
  1) On-call confirms signal source (trace id / customer prefix).
  2) Run: /infra reroute --prefix <prefix> --to fallback-region --mode canary  # moves 10% traffic then 100%
  3) Post a short status in #incidents and tag SRE lead.
  4) If reroute fails or error persists, escalate to oncall-sre-2 and open bridge.
Rollback: /infra reroute --prefix <prefix> --to primary-region
```

Carlos: One small nit — make the thresholds configurable per-customer. Some large customers overflow the metric windows. Maybe add an override flag in the runbook command like `--force` only for oncall leads.

Priya: Also propose adding a pre-check: if cached-KV-evictions > 30% in 2m then prefer reroute over scaling, because scaling takes too long.

Eli: I'm happy to own the runbook edit and push a PR. I'll also add a quick test script that simulates prefix-level load and verifies reroute command idempotency.

Jo: Postmortem — we should do a 45 minute session to go over timeline, customer impact, and acceptance criteria for the runbook change. Availability check: Thu 2026-03-18 16:00 PT or Fri 2026-03-19 10:00 PT.

Nina: Both options work for me. Can folks react with :thumbsup: for Thu or :eyes: for Fri so we can pick.

Carlos: :thumbsup:
Eli: :thumbsup:
Priya: :eyes:
Jo: :thumbsup:

Nina: Alright Thu it is. Action items: 
- Eli: PR for runbook + test script (due Tue 2026-03-16)
- Priya: Add metric pre-check lines and KV-eviction guidance to runbook (due Wed 2026-03-17)
- Carlos: Draft pager dedup policy and routing table changes (due Wed 2026-03-17)
- Nina: Schedule postmortem calendar invite and prepare timeline + incident log scrub (invite out by EOD today)

Eli: Quick callout on pager dedup: ops-bot currently routes based purely on alert rule ID. If multiple alert rules detect the same prefix, we should have alert grouping by prefix hash + window to suppress duplicates for 5m. I can add a config PR for ops-bot if we agree.

Carlos: Yes please — dedup by `prefix:window:signature` sounds good. Make it configurable per channel.

Priya: Will add the KV-eviction thresholds and an example query to the PR. Example metric query we used: `sum(rate(kv_evictions[2m])) by (prefix) / sum(rate(kv_capacity[2m])) by (prefix)`. Put that under the 'pre-checks' section.

Nina: Also — quick customer comms plan: we'll include a brief summary in the weekly ops digest and reach out to the 2 internal customers directly. Carlos can draft a short note to the product Liaisons.

Jo: On the postmortem agenda: timeline, customer impact, root cause (bulk-batch logic + hot partition), mitigations, runbook changes, pager config change, and follow-ups with owners + due dates.

incident-bot: Reminder scheduled: Postmortem INC-2026-314 · 2026-03-18T16:00PT · Zoom link: https://meet.redwood/pm-INC-2026-314 (placeholder)

Nina: Thanks all. Eli — ping me when the PR is up and I’ll review. Also add a short 'how to test locally' section so oncall can validate the reroute step during drills.

Eli: Will do. I'll post the PR link in this thread when ready.

ops-bot: Scheduled maintenance window proposed: 2026-03-20 02:00UTC for tiny traffic-shift tests. Reply `ack` to accept.

Priya: ack

Carlos: ack

Nina: ack

Eli: PR posted: https://git.redwood/repo/reroute-runbook/pull/78 (mock link) — includes test, metric checks, and ops-bot dedup flag.

Nina: Reviewed and left comments. One remaining ask: add an explicit 'who to page' list for oncall-sre-2 when reroute fails.

Eli: Added that in commit and addressed comments. Marking this thread as the source of record for the runbook change.

Nina: Great. Closing the coordination thread — we'll capture final runbook text in the runbook repo and the postmortem doc. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. :heart:
